chapters.title: Define the maintenance decision and warning horizon first
One pump, one bearing, competing explanations
Baselines, simple rules and asset identity
Measurement, sampling and safe OT access
Edge outages, timing, data contracts and security
From features and model choice to approved work

takeaways: Start predictive maintenance with the maintenance decision and the warning horizon it needs, separating preparation time for spares, permits and access from hands-on repair time.

A model is only as good as the evidence chain behind it: a specific failure mode, suitable sensors and sampling, stable asset identities, trustworthy timestamps, data contracts and honest maintenance records.

Compare any model against existing practice and simple rules, test it at the level of maintenance events and lead time, and route warnings through human review into approved work orders before scaling.
hook: Predictive maintenance on Azure only pays off when a warning arrives early enough for your team to act on it. This episode is for maintenance managers, reliability engineers, OT and IT architects and data teams in manufacturing, and follows one hypothetical pump from sensor reading to approved work order to show which decisions, evidence, data and processes you need before choosing a model.
